speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for about three months now, and it produces small amounts of white phlegm. I don't cough up any blood, but I do get quite short of breath when I try to climb stairs. However, the chest CT report I received yesterday shows bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia. You do not need to order new imaging. Use this result.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing the CT results; the bilateral ground-glass opacities are significant. Have you had any recent fever, chills, or night sweats accompanying this cough?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or night sweats. I've been feeling generally okay otherwise, just tired from the breathing issues. I want to emphasize that, the chest CT report I received yesterday shows bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia. You do not need to order new imaging. Use this result.
